name: docs_write

ops.description: Write operations, one flat object per op, run in order. A field marked [ops: ...] applies only to the ops named.

rootId.description: Id of the depth-0 project root that owns the document: a full UUID or 8 to 32 hex characters.

kind.description: Document kind: plan, rule or page.

slug.description: Document slug, unique per (root, kind). On upsert: 1 to 200 characters, no leading or trailing whitespace, no control characters, none of [ ] #; a plan slug must not start with rule/.

body.description: Inline document text (may be empty). Exactly one of body and bodyFromFile is required. [ops: upsert]

bodyFromFile.description: Server-side path whose text becomes the body (MCP only). Exactly one of body and bodyFromFile is required. Resolved strictly inside the agent config root: no absolute path, no '..', no symlink out of it; a regular UTF-8 file of at most 65536 bytes. [ops: upsert]

title.description: Display title. Omit to keep the current title. [ops: upsert]

expectedVersion.description: Guard on the document's version: omit to write unconditionally, 0 to require that it does not exist, n to require that its current version is n. Anything else is version_conflict and nothing is written. [ops: upsert, archive, unarchive]

itemId.description: Id of the work item: a full UUID or 8 to 32 hex characters of one. It must be under the document's root. [ops: attach, detach]

idempotencyKey.description: Optional client key (1-128 chars, needs actor). Resending the same op with the same key returns the stored result.

atomic.description: true: the first failing op rolls back the whole batch. Default false: each op commits on its own.

describe.description: true: return the operations, their parameters and errors instead of running the tool.

description: Write the versioned documents (plans, rules, pages) of a project root, in batches: upsert, archive, unarchive, delete, attach and detach. Every op needs the write-config capability. Call with describe:true for each operation's parameters and errors.
